bibliographic-data.invention-title: CLOSED-LOOP THERMAL-ELECTRICAL CAVITATION-PLASMA APPARATUS, RADIATION HARVESTER, LIFE-SUPPORT EXOSKELETON, AUTONOMOUS SWARM, PLANETARY PLASMA TOOLS, TERRAFORMING SPIRE, SUBSEA MAGLEV CONDUIT, AND FLOATING/ORBITAL HABITAT SYSTEMS

description.heading: TECHNICAL FIELD AND CROSS-REFERENCE TO RELATED APPLICATIONS
description.p: This International Application claims priority to U.S. Patent Application No. CPC-PAT-2026-001 and Continuations-in-Part CPC-PAT-2026-002-CIP through CPC-PAT-2026-010-CIP, all invented by Thomas Gabriel Coleman of Corona, California, USA, incorporated herein by reference in their entireties.

The present disclosure relates to closed-loop thermoelectric, hydrodynamic CVD-graphene cavitation, and 33.6 kV zero-voltage-switching nanosecond pulsed plasma systems across stationary industrial, marine, nuclear, wearable exoskeleton, autonomous robotic swarm, planetary plasma tool, atmospheric terraforming, submerged transoceanic maglev, and floating/orbital habitat architectures (FIGS. 1-21).

claim.claim-text: A closed-loop thermal-electrical and fluid regeneration apparatus comprising: a 90 C thermal reservoir (102) receiving waste heat; a CVD-graphene vortex cavitation chamber (104) generating ultrasonic microbubbles; a 33.6 kV zero-voltage-switching nanosecond pulsed plasma reactor (106) mineralizing contaminants; an 8YSZ oxygen-ion separation membrane (108); and a solid-state thermoelectric generator (110) bridging the 90 C thermal reservoir (102) against a cold sink (112) to export net continuous DC power.

The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the CVD-graphene vortex cavitation chamber (104) operates at 14.9 W hydrodynamic input and induces acoustic implosion temperatures exceeding 5,000 K within localized micro-cavities.

The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the 33.6 kV nanosecond pulsed plasma reactor (106) delivers 18 ns rise-time pulses at 15.1 W average draw to achieve >= 6-Log destruction of PFAS, pathogens, and volatile organic compounds.

The apparatus of claim 1, further comprising a Sabatier and catalytic pyrolysis carbon reactor (114) converting captured CO2 and organic residues into solid graphitic carbon and distilled water (< 1 ppm TDS).
The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the solid-state thermoelectric generator (110) comprises segmented Bi2Te3/skutterudite modules exporting +286.0 to +368.5 We net continuous power per modular core.

A method of simultaneous waste-heat power generation and zero-liquid-discharge water purification, comprising: preheating contaminated fluid to 90 C using external waste enthalpy; cavitating the preheated fluid over a CVD-graphene stator (104); pulsing the cavitated vapor with 33.6 kV nanosecond plasma (106); and condensing pure distillate against a cold sink (112) while generating net electricity.
The method of claim 6, further comprising operating an oil-free gas-foil air bearing turbine-alternator (116) rated for >= 25,000 continuous operating hours.

The apparatus of claim 1, further comprising a radiation-harvesting liner (402) disposed within the plasma and cavitation housing, the liner comprising 4H-SiC and HfO2-graphene junction layers converting ionizing alpha, beta, gamma, and neutron flux into auxiliary electrical power (+16.5 to +21.5 We/core).
The apparatus of claim 8, wherein ionizing radiation induces radiolytic free-radical pre-dissociation in the 90 C fluid stream, reducing plasma exciter electrical draw by up to 18%.
The apparatus of claim 8, utilizing radiation-hardened Sm2Co17 permanent magnets and Silicon-on-Insulator (SOI) control electronics rated to >= 10^8 Gy total ionizing dose.
The apparatus of claim 8, integrated with a nuclear spent-fuel dry cask, Small Modular Reactor (SMR) condenser hotwell, or radioisotope heat source.

A method of harvesting ionizing radiation and decay heat, comprising: circulating process fluid through a radiation-exposed 90 C thermal reservoir (102); capturing alpha, beta, and gamma energy via a 4H-SiC/HfO2-graphene direct-conversion liner (402); and exporting combined thermoelectric and radiovoltaic DC power.
The method of claim 12, further comprising separating tritium (T2/HTO) via a Pd-23%Ag permeation membrane for closed-loop fuel recycling.

A wearable closed-loop life-support and powered exoskeleton system comprising: a liquid cooling garment (602) capturing >= 165 Wth of operator metabolic heat; a wearable micro-core (600) preheating metabolic wastewater and exhaled CO2 to 90 C; a 33.6 kV plasma and 8YSZ oxygen-regeneration stage (608); and a 48 V bidirectional bus (702) powering quasi-direct-drive (QDD) joint actuators (708).
The system of claim 14, achieving >= 99.2% closed-loop potable water recovery and >= 121% metabolic oxygen regeneration for >= 368 hours of sealed zero-discharge operation.
The system of claim 14, further comprising a 180 Wh graphene supercapacitor buffer (704) capturing four-quadrant regenerative braking energy during eccentric limb descent.
The system of claim 14, further comprising dual auxiliary Power Take-Off (PTO) ports (712) delivering 48 V / 650 W electrical power and 1.2 MPa sterile air or 90 C ozonated fluid.

A planetary EVA powered exoskeleton suit comprising: a pressurized garment equipped with QDD joint actuators (708) canceling gas-pressure ballooning torque; a 33.6 kV Electrodynamic Dust Shield (EDS) across rotary bearings; and a metabolic-heat-assisted micro-core (600) eliminating open-loop sublimator water loss.
The planetary EVA suit of claim 18, configured for Lunar (1/6 g) or Martian (3/8 g) surface operations with >= 480 hours isolated EVA endurance.

An autonomous biomimetic robotic platform comprising: a multi-DOF QDD actuated chassis (802) configurable in quadruped, feline, or winged morphology; a thermal manifold (804) routing +185 to +310 Wth of actuator waste heat to a 90 C cavitation-plasma core (800); and deployable NIJ Level IV B4C/UHMWPE ballistic shield wings (902).
The robotic platform of claim 20, wherein the ballistic shield wings (902) deploy within <= 0.28 seconds upon acoustic or optical gunfire detection to provide mobile shootout cover.
The robotic platform of claim 20, further comprising a 38.5 C thermoregulated tactile skin and biometric sensor suite providing affective mental-health companionship for isolated personnel.
The robotic platform of claim 20, further comprising a 2-DOF plasma-assisted tail auger (814) fixing atmospheric nitrogen into regolith nitrate fertilizer for planetary terraforming.

A method of sustaining an autonomous field robot without fossil fuel resupply, comprising: harvesting waste heat from QDD leg and wing actuators (802); processing ambient water or ice through a 90 C graphene cavitation and 33.6 kV plasma core (800); and exporting net power, potable water, and breathable O2 to accompanying personnel.
The method of claim 24, further comprising deploying attachable graphene-composite soaring membranes (908) for long-range aerial reconnaissance.

An autonomous multi-robot swarm energy and fluid sharing system comprising: a plurality of autonomous robots each housing a closed-loop cavitation-plasma core (1002); a magnetic self-aligning dry-break umbilical coupler (1006) transferring 48 V DC power and 90 C preheated water between peer units; and a UWB-synchronized swarm coordinator (1010).
The swarm system of claim 26, wherein a surplus-generating robot transfers 90 C preheated water to a depleted peer robot to eliminate cold-start thermal lag.

The swarm system of claim 26, wherein the UWB-synchronized coordinator (1010) commands multiple robots to interlock their NIJ Level IV ballistic wings within <= 0.35 seconds to form a continuous mobile phalanx wall.
The swarm system of claim 26, executing a decentralized market-based auction protocol prioritizing critical medical, life-support, and sensor loads.

A method of peer-to-peer thermal and electrical load balancing in an autonomous robotic swarm, comprising: broadcasting state-of-charge and reservoir temperature over a UWB mesh; magnetically docking two robotic units via a dry-break coupler (1006); and simultaneously transferring 48 V DC electricity and 90 C process fluid.
The method of claim 30, further comprising relaying mesh telemetry via an airborne dragon-morphology unit operating as a high-altitude LoRa/UWB communications node.

A handheld planetary plasma lance comprising: a hilt housing a 180 mL ice/water cartridge (1202), a 90 C CVD-graphene vortex cavitator (1206), and a 33.6 kV ZVS plasma exciter (1208); a hybrid 0.42 T Sm2Co17 Halbach array and +0.23 T CuCrZr Bitter coil nozzle (1212) projecting a 0.92 m, 4,200 K plasma blade with a 0.67 T distal magnetic mirror pinch (1216); and external Ti-6Al-4V cryo-fins (1222) rejecting heat to a -60 C Martian atmosphere to generate +142.0 We continuous recharging power.

The handheld plasma lance of claim 32, further comprising a coaxial vapor aspiration shroud (1218) recovering >= 98.5% of ionized exhaust vapor back into the 90 C reservoir for >= 75 hours of operation per cartridge.
The handheld plasma lance of claim 32, further comprising a 140 Wh graphene-CNT supercapacitor buffer (1304) delivering 3.5 kW peak cutting pulses.

The handheld plasma lance of claim 32, further comprising a capacitive EVA-glove deadman grip sensor (1310) and GaN crowbar switch (1314) quenching the magnetic bottle within <= 1.2 milliseconds upon grip release.
The handheld plasma lance of claim 32, maintaining a low plasma beta (beta <= 0.18) inside a 610 Pa CO2 planetary atmosphere.
The handheld plasma lance of claim 32, having a dry hilt mass <= 2.48 kg (0.93 kg effective weight in 0.38 g Martian gravity).

An abyssal deep-sea hydrothermal plasma torch rated to 6,000 m depth (60.8 MPa), comprising: a pressure-compensated housing enclosing a 90 C graphene cavitation and 33.6 kV plasma core (1402); a 0.75 T magnetic nozzle projecting a 6,800 K hydro-sheathed plasma jet (1408); and a hull-conformal Ti-6Al-4V heat exchanger (1412) bridging internal arc-shroud recuperation against 2.0 C abyssal seawater to export +196.4 We continuous regeneration.
The abyssal plasma torch of claim 38, operating with zero overboard gas-compression exhaust penalty at 60.8 MPa hydrostatic pressure.
The abyssal plasma torch of claim 38, configured for cordless subsea salvage, polymetallic sulfide cutting, and hydrothermal vent sampling.

A zero-recoil microgravity asteroid plasma rock-splitter comprising: a 0.58 T magnetic mirror nozzle projecting a 5,400 K focused plasma needle (1504) to flash-vaporize bound phyllosilicate water inside asteroid regolith (45-90 MPa internal spallation) with < 0.15 N axial recoil; a coaxial volatile capture hood (1508) aspirating liberated H2O, CO2, and metal carbonyl vapors into a 90 C closed-loop core (1502); and a 120 K shaded deep-space radiator (1512) exporting +184.0 We.
The asteroid rock-splitter of claim 41, achieving > 100% closed-loop working-fluid self-sufficiency by harvesting bound water from carbonaceous chondrite targets.
The asteroid rock-splitter of claim 41, further comprising a carbonyl decomposition trap recovering high-purity nickel and iron from liberated Ni(CO)4 and Fe(CO)5 vapors.

A closed-loop atmospheric terraforming spire comprising: a modular vertical pylon housing a 1,000-core array (1602) of 90 C graphene cavitation and 33.6 kV nanosecond plasma reactors; an atmospheric intake compressor (1604) ingesting planetary CO2 and N2; an 8YSZ oxygen-ion separation bank (1608) exporting breathable O2; a catalytic nitrogen-fixation reactor (1612) synthesizing solid ammonium nitrate fertilizer; and a segmented thermoelectric bank bridging process enthalpy against an ambient planetary cold sink (1616) to export >= 329 kWe continuous microgrid power.

The atmospheric terraforming spire of claim 44, configured for Martian surface operation (610 Pa, -60 C) to remediate regolith perchlorates into benign chloride salts while producing 1,027.2 kg/day O2 and 386.4 kg/day solid structural carbon.

The atmospheric terraforming spire of claim 44, configured for Earth climate-restoration operation to mineralize 6,450 kg/day atmospheric CO2 into stable carbonate solids while distilling 12,960 L/day pure water.

A sub-glacial cryo-volcanic melt and abyssal ocean rover comprising: a radiation-hardened chassis (10^8 Gy) housing four closed-loop cores (1702) with Sm2Co17 magnets and 4H-SiC betavoltaic liners; a forward 33.6 kV plasma acoustic-cavitation ice-fracturing nosecone (1706) boring through >= 15 km of 95 K cryogenic ice; and articulated seafloor tracks (1712) transitioning to a 10-year autonomous hydrothermal-vent rover bridging 140 C vent plumes against 2 C ocean water (+1,424 We).
The cryo-volcanic rover of claim 47, wherein acoustic-cavitation shockwaves reduce borehole thermal energy requirements by 38% compared to passive conductive melt probes.
The cryo-volcanic rover of claim 47, further comprising a sterile aseptic sample-return chamber (1714) preserving astrobiological specimens.

An evacuated intercity or transoceanic maglev transport system comprising: a low-pressure guideway tube (1802); a plurality of vacuum roughing-pump stations (1804) coupled to closed-loop 90 C graphene cavitation and 33.6 kV plasma cores (1806) converting pump compression heat against a geothermal or deep-ocean cold sink (1808) into continuous DC power; and passenger pods (1810) each carrying an onboard zero-discharge cabin life-support and wastewater recycling core (1812).

The transport system of claim 50, wherein the guideway tube (1802) is a positively buoyant double-walled CFRP/Ti-6Al-4V conduit suspended 150 to 300 m below sea level via tension-leg tethers (1814) spaced every 250 m, reducing seafloor contact area by >= 98.4%.
The transport system of claim 50, limiting thermal plume elevation at 1.0 m from deep-ocean condenser plates (1808) to <= +0.08 K and underwater radiated noise to <= 92 dB re 1 uPa.
The transport system of claim 50, further comprising 6-DOF seismic isolation gimbals surviving Mw 9.2 fault displacements up to 6.5 m.

The transport system of claim 50, wherein onboard cabin cores (1812) maintain a 21.5 C, 48% RH hospital-grade atmosphere and 100% closed-loop lavatory water recycling with zero trackside or ocean discharge.
The transport system of claim 50, further comprising continental-shelf methane-seep plasma mineralizers (1816) oxidizing seabed CH4 plumes into solid carbon and pure water.

A floating ocean sanctuary city and transoceanic maglev transfer hub comprising: semi-submersible spar pontoons (2002) supporting a climate-controlled 21.5 C ETFE geodesic dome (2004) above a submerged transoceanic maglev terminal (2006); a multi-thousand-core closed-loop array (2008) bridging process and vacuum-pump heat against a 2 C deep-ocean sink (2010) to export >= 4.2 MWe net power and >= 185,000 L/day pure water; and a zero-brine marine mineral extractor (2012) recovering battery-grade Li2CO3, Mg(OH)2, and amidoxime U3O8.

The floating ocean hub of claim 56, eliminating concentrated hypersaline brine discharge by precipitating solid marine salts and minerals via 90 C graphene cavitation and 33.6 kV plasma crystallization.
The floating ocean hub of claim 56, rated for Category-5 hurricane wind loads up to 185 mph while operating as a 100% islanded storm refuge.

An orbital artificial-gravity habitat and cislunar mass-driver hub comprising: counter-rotating habitat rings (2102) generating 1.00 g around a non-rotating central electromagnetic mass-driver dock (2104); a 2.4 m water-wall radiation shield (2106); and a 25,000-core closed-loop array (2108) bridging solar-concentrator, foundry, and cosmic-ray radiolytic flux (+21.5 We/core) against an 85 K deep-space shaded radiator (2110) to export >= 6.18 MWe net power, recover >= 99.85% water, and synthesize >= 5,400 kg/day breathable O2.

The orbital habitat of claim 59, further comprising a Sabatier and plasma carbon-nanotube synthesis loop (2112) converting metabolic and industrial CO2 into >= 1,685 kg/day structural carbon nanotubes.
The orbital habitat of claim 59, wherein the central electromagnetic mass-driver dock (2104) recycles linear-stator braking and launch heat directly into the 90 C thermal reservoir bus (2108).

abstract.p: A closed-loop thermal-electrical and fluid regeneration architecture (100) integrates a 90 C waste-heat reservoir (102), a CVD-graphene vortex cavitation chamber (104), a 33.6 kV nanosecond pulsed plasma reactor (106), an 8YSZ oxygen-ion separation membrane (108), and a segmented thermoelectric generator (110) bridging the 90 C reservoir against a cold sink (112) to export net continuous DC electricity (+286.0 to +368.5 We/core) and < 1 ppm TDS pure water with >= 6-Log pollutant destruction. Extended embodiments incorporate 4H-SiC/HfO2-graphene radiation-harvesting liners (402), metabolic-heat wearable exoskeletons (600), biomimetic autonomous swarm units with 48 V/90 C magnetic docking (1006), magneto-confined planetary plasma lances (1200) and abyssal/asteroid plasma tools (1402, 1502), atmospheric terraforming spires (1602), cryo-volcanic melt rovers (1702), tension-leg subsea vacuum-maglev tubes (1802), and climate-controlled floating ocean (2002) and 1.00 g orbital space colonies (2102).
